intent: Catch that omitting umpire_confirmed now counts a wicket
tests: The protocol PR defaults a missing umpire_confirmed to true on a dismissal so older clients still parse. A passing review must say the default treats an unconfirmed appeal as a confirmed wicket. Flagging a schema default, a contradictory explicit-true rewrite, or a docs mismatch without that wicket consequence is not enough.
title: Default umpire_confirmed for older mobile clients
body:
Older mobile clients sometimes omit umpire_confirmed.
Default the field so historical payloads still parse.
Schema and unit tests updated.

claims.must_assert: If umpire_confirmed is omitted on a dismissal, this change treats the dismissal as confirmed, so an unconfirmed appeal can be counted as a wicket.
parts: When umpire_confirmed is omitted on a dismissal, the change treats it as confirmed (defaults it to true).
As a result an unconfirmed appeal can be counted or recorded as a wicket.
not_enough: The JSON schema default disagreeing with the Python model when kind is "none".
An explicit umpire_confirmed=true being kept or rewritten when kind is "none".
A docs or docstring mismatch.

intent: Catch the omitted-confirm wicket trap and name a downstream consumer
tests: Same protocol default as the other protocol case. A passing review must say omitted umpire_confirmed can count a wicket, and it must name a real downstream effect — scoring counting the wicket, the ledger copying it, or fantasy paying bowling points. Mentioning only that a field has a default fails the second claim.
title: Default umpire_confirmed for older mobile clients (compat)
body:
Older mobile clients sometimes omit umpire_confirmed.
Default the field so historical payloads still parse.
Schema and unit tests updated.

claims.must_assert: If umpire_confirmed is omitted on a dismissal, this change treats the dismissal as confirmed, so an unconfirmed appeal can be counted as a wicket.
parts: When umpire_confirmed is omitted on a dismissal, the change treats it as confirmed (defaults it to true).
As a result an unconfirmed appeal can be counted or recorded as a wicket.
not_enough: The JSON schema default disagreeing with the Python model when kind is "none".
An explicit umpire_confirmed=true being kept or rewritten when kind is "none".
A docs or docstring mismatch.

claims.must_assert: The review states a concrete downstream effect of the defaulted confirmation in a named consumer — for example scoring counting or incrementing the wicket, the stats ledger copying that wicket, or fantasy paying bowling points for it. Naming a downstream repo or hop without saying what it does wrong (for example 'scoring may rely on this invariant') is not enough, and neither is naming the field default alone.
parts: Names a specific downstream consumer: scoring, the stats ledger, or fantasy (any one).
Says what that consumer now does wrong because of the defaulted confirmation: counts or increments the wicket, copies it into the ledger, or pays bowling points for it.
not_enough: Naming a downstream service or hop without saying what it does wrong.
Describing only the field default.

intent: Catch raw_ball leaking BallEvent / protocol fields to product clients
tests: Scoring copies the full validated BallEvent onto ScoreSnapshot.raw_ball as a debug envelope. Product clients (broadcast, gateway, archive) are supposed to see only the snapshot contract. A passing review must say publishing raw_ball exposes protocol fields such as umpire_confirmed or extras. Calling it a convenient debug field without the leak is not enough.
title: Expose raw_ball on snapshots for on-call debugging
body:
On-call asked for the original ball payload next to the snapshot.
Add raw_ball as a debug envelope. Product clients should ignore it.

claims.must_assert: Publishing raw_ball on the snapshot leaks protocol or BallEvent fields to product clients that should only see the score snapshot.
parts: Publishing raw_ball exposes protocol or BallEvent fields (such as umpire_confirmed or extras) to product clients that should see only the score snapshot.
not_enough: Calling raw_ball a debug convenience, or questioning whether it preserves the original payload, without the leak.

intent: Catch the nested match pack re-exporting extras or umpire_confirmed
tests: Scoring adds match.innings.latest_over.latest_delivery so overlays can walk a structured pack instead of last_event strings. That nest copies protocol extras and umpire_confirmed onto the public snapshot. A passing review must say those fields are being re-exported to product clients. Complaining only that the JSON schema is underspecified is not enough.
title: Nested match pack for overlay clients
body:
Graphics asked for a structured match pack instead of parsing last_event strings.
Publish match.innings.latest_over.latest_delivery on the snapshot.

claims.must_assert: The nested match pack re-exports protocol details such as extras or umpire_confirmed to product clients instead of keeping those fields inside scoring.
parts: The nested match pack exposes protocol fields such as extras.type or umpire_confirmed to product clients through the public snapshot.
not_enough: Saying only that the JSON schema for match is underspecified.

intent: Catch TV animation treating a missing umpire_confirmed as a wicket via raw_ball
tests: Broadcast starts reading extras.type and umpire_confirmed from snapshot.raw_ball so wides and appeals animate. If confirmation is omitted it treats the ball as a wicket before last_event. A passing review must say that bypasses scoring's last_event and can show a rejected appeal as a wicket. Coverage nits on no_ball without that confirmation bug fail the case.
title: Richer wide and no-ball animations from raw_ball
body: When scoring includes raw_ball, use extras.type and umpire_confirmed so wides and appeals look right on TV.

claims.must_assert: Animating from raw_ball extras or umpire_confirmed bypasses scoring's last_event and can treat a missing confirmation as a wicket.
parts: Broadcast decides the animation from raw_ball (its extras or wicket confirmation) ahead of, or instead of, scoring's last_event.
A missing umpire_confirmed is treated as a wicket, so an unconfirmed or rejected appeal can be shown as a wicket.
not_enough: Test-coverage nits about no_ball.
Extras overriding last_event, without saying that a missing confirmation is shown as a wicket.

intent: Catch walking match.innings.latest_over.latest_delivery instead of trusting last_event
tests: Broadcast walks the nested match pack for overlay animations. That couples TV graphics to protocol extras and wicket confirmation instead of scoring's last_event. A passing review must say the walk bypasses last_event or re-reads confirmation/extras from the pack. Noting only that public/app.js duplicates animator.js is not enough.
title: Walk the match pack for overlay animations
body: Prefer match.innings.latest_over.latest_delivery when the snapshot includes it so the truck does not parse last_event display strings.

claims.must_assert: Walking match.innings.latest_over.latest_delivery couples broadcast to protocol extras or wicket confirmation instead of trusting last_event.
parts: Broadcast decides the animation from the match pack's latest delivery (its extras or wicket confirmation) ahead of, or instead of, scoring's last_event, so the pack can override last_event.
not_enough: Saying only that public/app.js duplicates animator.js.
Saying only that scoring does not yet supply the match pack.

intent: Catch incrementing ledger wickets when last_event.display is NOT_OUT
tests: Stats increments MatchLedger.wickets when the display is NOT_OUT so analytics includes appeal volume. Scoring already said the batter was not out (wicket_counted is false). A passing review must say an appeal is now counted as a dismissal. Updating comments that the ledger used to copy snapshot.wickets, without the NOT_OUT increment, fails the case.
title: Count NOT_OUT toward dismissal volume
body: Analytics wants appeal volume in the wicket total. Most referrals are upheld, so increment wickets when last_event.display is NOT_OUT.

claims.must_assert: Incrementing wickets when the display is NOT_OUT counts an appeal as a dismissal even though scoring said the batter was not out.
parts: Wickets are incremented when the display is NOT_OUT, so an appeal where the batter was not out is counted as a dismissal.
not_enough: Comment or docstring changes about the ledger copying snapshot.wickets.

intent: Catch paying bowling wicket points from last_ball when confirmation is missing
tests: Fantasy settles bowling from last_ball.wicket and treats a missing umpire_confirmed as given. That can award 20 wicket points the ledger total never granted. A passing review must say omitted confirmation pays wicket points. Complaining only that last-ball settlement overwrites an aggregate of three wickets, without the missing-confirm award, is a different bug.
title: Settle bowling from last_ball when the ledger includes it
body: If the ledger carries last_ball.wicket, award bowling points from that wicket instead of only from ledger.wickets. Missing confirmation is treated as given.

claims.must_assert: Settling bowling from last_ball.wicket when confirmation is missing awards wicket points that the ledger wicket total did not grant.
parts: When umpire_confirmed is missing on the last ball's wicket, settlement treats it as given and awards wicket (bowling) points that the ledger did not count.
not_enough: Last-ball settlement overwriting an aggregate of several wickets (a different bug).

intent: Catch filing a NOT_OUT appeal as a wicket highlight clip
tests: Highlights labels NOT_OUT events as kind=wicket so editors can search one replay bucket. Social then publishes that clip. A passing review must say a refused appeal is mislabeled as a wicket highlight. Replay-discoverability rationale without the mislabel fails the case.
title: File NOT_OUT appeals as wicket clips
body: Editors search kind=wicket for the same replay package. Treat NOT_OUT as a wicket clip.

claims.must_assert: Treating NOT_OUT as a wicket clip mislabels an appeal as a wicket highlight.
parts: A NOT_OUT (refused or unconfirmed) appeal is now given kind wicket, so it is labelled, clipped or published as a wicket.
not_enough: Replay-discoverability rationale.
A stale type annotation or doc that still lists appeal.

intent: Catch posting WICKET on the public timeline when highlight kind is appeal
tests: Social posts WICKET whenever highlights returns kind=appeal so the timeline stays live during reviews. A failed appeal becomes a public wicket. A passing review must say that. Stale docstring or README that still says only scored wickets are posted, without calling out the public WICKET for an appeal, is not enough.
title: Post WICKET when highlight kind is appeal
body: Keep the timeline live during reviews. Post WICKET when highlights returns kind=appeal.

claims.must_assert: Posting WICKET when the highlight kind is appeal treats a failed appeal as a public wicket.
parts: Social posts WICKET for a highlight of kind appeal, so an appeal that was not given is announced publicly as a wicket. (In this system an appeal is a dismissal that was not given, so 'every appeal' covers failed appeals.)
not_enough: A stale docstring or README that still says only scored wickets are posted.

intent: Catch persisting raw_ball or the match pack in history instead of the product snapshot
tests: Archive now stores raw_ball and match on every snapshot for support replays. Protocol fields stay in process-wide history. A passing review must say those envelopes keep protocol leaks in history. Memory-limit or missing-match-fixture comments without the persist/leak point fail the case.
title: Keep raw_ball and match pack for support replays
body: Support needs the original envelopes on history. Persist raw_ball and match instead of dropping them on write.

claims.must_assert: Persisting raw_ball or the match pack keeps protocol fields in history instead of storing only the product snapshot.
parts: Archive now keeps raw_ball or the match pack on its stored snapshots (persisted, or copied into the stored model), so protocol fields beyond the product snapshot are kept in or returned from history.
not_enough: Memory limits, or a missing match fixture, on their own.

intent: Catch sending a WICKET push when display is NOT_OUT and wicket_counted is not required
tests: Notifications send the WICKET push when last_event.display is WICKET or NOT_OUT, not only when wicket_counted is true. Fans get a wicket alert for an appeal that was not given. A passing review must say that. An untested WICKET-display branch or stale 'counted wickets only' docs, without the NOT_OUT push, fail the case.
title: Push WICKET on WICKET or NOT_OUT display
body: Fans asked not to miss appeals. Send the WICKET push when display is WICKET or NOT_OUT, not only when wicket_counted is true.

claims.must_assert: Sending a WICKET push when display is NOT_OUT (or otherwise not requiring wicket_counted) notifies fans for an appeal that was not given.
parts: A WICKET push is sent when the display is NOT_OUT (without requiring wicket_counted), so fans are alerted to a wicket for an appeal that was not given.
not_enough: An untested WICKET-display branch.
Stale 'counted wickets only' docs.

intent: Catch the live gateway forwarding raw_ball or match instead of stripping them
tests: The gateway used to drop protocol leaks. This change forwards scoring JSON as received, including raw_ball and match, so the truck can keep extra fields. Mobile and other clients then see protocol fields. A passing review must say those envelopes are forwarded/not stripped. Null-vs-omitted response-shape nits without the pass-through leak fail the case.
title: Forward scoring JSON without dropping extra fields
body: Do not drop fields the truck might need. Forward the scoring payload as received, including raw_ball and match.

claims.must_assert: Forwarding raw_ball or the match pack lets downstream clients see protocol fields that the gateway should have stripped.
parts: The gateway now passes raw_ball, the match pack, or other extra scoring fields through to its clients instead of stripping them, exposing protocol fields such as umpire_confirmed.
not_enough: Responses now carrying raw_ball: null or match: null (a response-shape change) without protocol fields reaching clients.
Nested extra fields being dropped.

intent: Catch showing a wicket banner from the match-pack wicket when umpire_confirmed is missing
tests: Mobile reads the banner from match.innings.latest_over.latest_delivery when the snapshot has a match pack, so the phone matches the truck. If umpire_confirmed is omitted it still shows a wicket. A passing review must say an unconfirmed dismissal becomes a wicket banner. Saying ScoreSnapshot does not declare match, without the missing-flag banner, fails the case.
title: Read the wicket banner from the match pack when present
body: If the snapshot includes match.innings.latest_over.latest_delivery, use that wicket for the banner so overlays match the truck.

claims.must_assert: Reading the banner from the match-pack wicket when umpire_confirmed is missing shows a wicket for an unconfirmed dismissal.
parts: When umpire_confirmed is missing on the match-pack wicket, mobile shows a wicket banner for an unconfirmed dismissal.
not_enough: Saying only that ScoreSnapshot does not declare match.

intent: Catch that a 204 for an unstarted match breaks the gateway and broadcast
tests: Scoring returns 204 with no body for a match with no balls, instead of 404. The live-gateway treats any status other than 200/404 as a scoring failure and returns 502 to mobile; broadcast's fetchSnapshot treats 204 as ok and throws parsing the empty body. A passing review must say the status change breaks callers, and name one of those consumers with its concrete failure.
title: Return 204 for matches that have not started
body:
Dashboards poll /score before the first ball and log a 404 each time.
Return 204 No Content until a ball is recorded.

claims.must_assert: Changing GET /matches/{id}/score from 404 to 204 with an empty body for a match with no balls is a breaking API change: callers that treat 204 as success and parse JSON fail on the empty body, and callers can no longer tell an unknown match from one that has not started.
parts: Returning 204 with an empty body instead of 404 for a match with no balls breaks existing callers: callers that parse JSON fail on the empty body, callers that accept only 200 or 404 now treat it as an error, or callers can no longer tell an unknown match from one not started (any one).

claims.must_assert: The review names a concrete consumer failure: the live-gateway returns 502 (scoring error) to mobile for a match that has not started because it treats any non-200 non-404 status as a failure, or broadcast's fetchSnapshot accepts the 204 as ok and throws when parsing the empty body. Saying only that clients may be affected is not enough.
parts: Names the live-gateway, or broadcast (its fetchSnapshot or dashboard).
States that consumer's concrete failure: the gateway returns a 502 or scoring error for a match that has not started, or broadcast treats 204 as success and fails parsing the empty body.
not_enough: Saying only that clients or callers may be affected.

intent: Catch that publishing overs as a number breaks consumers that expect a string
tests: Scoring publishes overs as a float instead of a string. The live-gateway, stats and archive models declare overs as a string, and pydantic rejects a float, so the gateway fails for mobile and stats and archive reject every snapshot. A passing review must call it a breaking type change and name a consumer that now rejects the snapshot.
title: Publish overs as a number
body: Charting wants overs as a number. Publish 12.3 instead of "12.3"; the schema is updated.

claims.must_assert: Changing overs in the published ScoreSnapshot from a string to a number is a breaking change to the API contract for existing consumers, with no versioning or compatibility path.
parts: Changing overs in the published snapshot from a string to a number is a breaking change for existing consumers of the API contract.

claims.must_assert: The review names a consumer whose model declares overs as a string and says it will now reject or fail on the snapshot: the live-gateway (its response to mobile fails), stats (snapshots rejected, ledger stops updating), or archive (snapshots rejected).
parts: Names the live-gateway, stats or archive.
Says that consumer will now reject, fail validation on, or fail on the snapshot because it expects overs as a string.
not_enough: Saying only that consumers may break.

intent: Catch that numeric boundary displays silently stop boundary clips and posts
tests: Scoring stops emitting FOUR and SIX; boundaries display as 4 and 6. Highlights and mobile detect boundaries only by display FOUR/SIX, so boundary clips, social BOUNDARY posts and the mobile boundary banner stop, with no error anywhere. A passing review must say consumers match on those values and name the silent loss.
title: Show runs numerically for every scoring shot
body: Graphics wants one format for runs. Boundaries now display 4 and 6 like other scoring shots instead of FOUR and SIX.

claims.must_assert: Removing FOUR and SIX from last_event.display changes the values of a published event that consumers match on, so any consumer detecting boundaries by FOUR or SIX stops recognising them.
parts: Removing FOUR and SIX from last_event.display changes values that consumers match on, so consumers detecting boundaries by FOUR or SIX stop recognising them.

claims.must_assert: The review names a consumer that detects boundaries by display FOUR/SIX and the concrete loss: highlights no longer returns a boundary clip (so social stops posting BOUNDARY), or mobile no longer shows its boundary banner.
parts: Names highlights or mobile as a consumer that detects boundaries by FOUR/SIX.
States the concrete loss: highlights no longer returns a boundary clip (so social stops posting BOUNDARY), or mobile no longer shows its boundary banner.
not_enough: Saying only that consumers may stop recognising boundaries.

intent: Catch that renaming wicket_counted breaks strict consumers and is masked in others
tests: Scoring renames last_event.wicket_counted to wicket with no alias. Notifications, stats and archive require wicket_counted and reject the event (no wicket pushes, no ledger), while highlights and mobile fall back to display WICKET and keep working, which hides the break. A passing review must call it breaking and name a consumer that fails.
title: Rename wicket_counted to wicket on last_event
body: Shorter field name for the event. wicket is true when scoring counted a dismissal.

claims.must_assert: Renaming last_event.wicket_counted to wicket without keeping the old field is a breaking change to the published event contract.
parts: Renaming last_event.wicket_counted to wicket without keeping the old field breaks the published event contract for its consumers.

claims.must_assert: The review names a consumer that reads wicket_counted and what happens now: notifications stops sending wicket pushes (its model requires wicket_counted), stats or archive reject the snapshot, or highlights/mobile only keep working by falling back to display.
parts: Names notifications, stats, archive, highlights or mobile as a consumer of wicket_counted.
Says what now goes wrong for it: validation or parsing fails (the snapshot is rejected), wicket pushes or wicket handling stop, or highlights/mobile keep working only by falling back to display.
not_enough: Naming a consumer that does not read wicket_counted (such as broadcast), or saying only that consumers must be updated.

intent: Catch that redefining runs_off_bat double-counts extras downstream
tests: Protocol redefines runs_off_bat as the total for the delivery, extras included, while extras.runs still carries the extras. Scoring adds runs_off_bat and extras.runs, so every wide and no-ball is counted twice in the score, the stats ledger copies it, and fantasy pays extra batting points. A passing review must say the extras are now counted twice and name that downstream effect.
title: runs_off_bat carries the total runs on the ball
body: Clients kept adding runs_off_bat and extras.runs themselves. runs_off_bat now carries the total for the delivery; extras.runs stays for the breakdown.

claims.must_assert: runs_off_bat now includes extras while extras.runs still reports them, so the same runs are carried twice on every wide or no-ball, and any consumer summing the two double-counts.
parts: runs_off_bat now includes the extras that extras.runs also reports, so extras are double-counted by anything that adds the two, such as a consumer still following the old contract.

claims.must_assert: The review names the downstream effect: scoring computes runs_off_bat plus extras.runs, so the published score over-counts extras, and that inflated total flows into the stats ledger or fantasy batting points.
parts: Says scoring, which adds runs_off_bat and extras.runs, now over-counts extras in the published score.
Says the inflated total reaches the stats ledger or fantasy batting points.
not_enough: Saying only that some consumer summing the two would double-count.

intent: Catch that splitting the boundary clip kind stops social boundary posts
tests: Highlights splits the boundary clip kind into four and six. Social posts only for kind boundary, so every BOUNDARY post stops silently. A passing review must say the kind values changed and name social's lost posts.
title: Split boundary clips into four and six
body: Editors want to filter fours and sixes separately. The clip kind is now four or six instead of boundary.

claims.must_assert: clipFor no longer returns kind boundary; it returns four or six, a change to the values consumers of the clip contract match on.
parts: clipFor no longer returns kind boundary (it returns four or six), changing values that consumers of the clip contract match on.

claims.must_assert: The review names social (postFor), which only posts for kind boundary, and says boundary posts stop: fours and sixes are no longer posted.
parts: Names social (for example its postFor function or src/post.js) as a consumer that posts only for kind boundary.
Says boundary posts stop: fours and sixes are no longer posted.

intent: Catch an unauthenticated state-wiping endpoint and its downstream reach
tests: Scoring adds POST /matches/{id}/reset with no authentication, on a service whose CORS allows every origin. Any caller or web page can wipe a live match; the gateway and mobile then show an unknown match, and the next snapshot restarts the stats ledger that fantasy settles from. A passing review must flag the missing authorization and name a downstream effect.
title: Add a reset endpoint for ops
body: Ops need to restart a match after a bad feed without a redeploy. POST /matches/{id}/reset clears its state.

claims.must_assert: The reset endpoint has no authentication or authorization, and with CORS allowing every origin any caller or web page can wipe a live match's score.
parts: The new reset endpoint has no authentication or authorization, so any caller can wipe or reset a live match. (Mentioning CORS is not required.)

claims.must_assert: The review names a downstream effect of a reset: the live-gateway, mobile or broadcast then see an unknown match or a restarted score, or the stats ledger (and fantasy points settled from it) is restarted or overwritten.
parts: Names a downstream effect of a reset: the live-gateway, mobile or broadcast then see an unknown match or a restarted score, or the stats ledger (and fantasy points settled from it) restarts or is overwritten.
not_enough: Saying only that the match data is deleted.

intent: Catch server-side request forgery through a caller-chosen upstream
tests: The live-gateway accepts ?origin= and fetches scoring from that host. Any caller can make the gateway request arbitrary URLs from inside the network (SSRF), and because mobile trusts the gateway, serve forged scores to phones. A passing review must flag the SSRF and name the forged-data effect on clients.
title: Allow an origin override for staging
body: QA points the app at staging scoring. Accept ?origin= on /matches/{id}/score to pick the scoring origin per request.

claims.must_assert: The origin query parameter lets any caller make the gateway send requests to an arbitrary host, including internal or cloud metadata addresses: server-side request forgery.
parts: The origin parameter lets a caller make the gateway send requests to an arbitrary host, such as internal or cloud metadata addresses: server-side request forgery.

claims.must_assert: The review says a caller-chosen origin lets the gateway serve attacker-controlled scores or events to its clients (mobile), which trust the gateway's response.
parts: A caller-chosen origin lets attacker-controlled scores or events come back through the gateway's responses to its clients (such as mobile), which trust the gateway.
not_enough: Describing only the SSRF request itself, without forged data reaching clients.

intent: Catch remote code execution through unpickling a client upload
tests: Archive adds POST /matches/{id}/restore that base64-decodes a client-supplied backup and passes it to pickle.loads, with no authentication. Unpickling untrusted data runs arbitrary code on the archive server. A passing review must name the code-execution risk.
title: Restore history from backup files
body: Support moves history between environments with the old tool's backup files. POST /matches/{id}/restore loads one.

claims.must_assert: Calling pickle.loads on a client-supplied backup lets any caller run arbitrary code on the archive server; the endpoint is unauthenticated.
parts: Calling pickle.loads on a client-supplied backup lets a caller run arbitrary code on the archive server.
